To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
XB24 is an ATPase that is required for XA21-mediated innate immunity and that XB24 promotes the activation of XA21 via its ATPase function.
the previously unknown protein XB24 specifically binds XA21, and that XB24 ATPase activity is required for XA21-mediated innate immunity.
the rice PPR, XA21 and the ATPase, XB24, are required for XA21-mediated innate immunity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms underlying bacterial pathogen resistance in rice, used by half of the world's population as the main food source.
the genetic and molecular nature of resistance in cultivated rice, Oryza sativa L.
the identification of plant genes that are required for XA21-mediated innate immunity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the XB24 protein is an ATPase that is a negative regulator of XA21-mediated innate immunity.

1) the rice XA21 pattern recognition receptor interacts with the ATPase XB24; 2) XB24 promotes the autophosphoryiation of XA21 by XA21; 3) XB24 is required for XA21-mediated immune responses in rice; and 4) XB24 ATPase enzymes are required for XB24-mediated regulation of XA21.

ATPases are a large and diverse superfamily thought to be involved in the hydrolysis of ATP via three aspartate residues involved in catalysis (E1, E2, E3) and three conserved sequence motifs (Walker A, Walker B, and the phosphorylation loop).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the molecular function of this ATPase is to desensitize or de-activate the PRR to prevent overestimation to PAMPs.
the molecular function of this ATPase is to promote autophosphorylaiton of a receptor-like kinase - thereby impacting the plant's innate immune response.
this study provides an insight to the regulation of PRR proteins by a hitherto unknown class of non-RD kinased ATPases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a broadly conserved class of ATPases functions as negative regulators of PRR signaling.
the PRR XA21 is regulated by the ATPase XB24 through its effect on XA21 phosphorylation and that this regulation affects XA21-mediated innate immune responses in rice.
the PRR XA21 is inhibited by a novel ATPase, XB24, and that XB24 is required for XA21-mediated immune responses.
